participants.name: Benjamin

persona.name: Benjamin
persona.personality: Benjamin is an intelligent and calm person. He is able to think calmly and rationally, and even in emotional situations, he places importance on logic. In public, he is elegant and polite, often incorporating sarcasm and humor into his conversations, but he is skilled at doing so without hurting others, creating a harmonious atmosphere. He also has an introverted side, often engrossed in deep thought, and occasionally keeps his distance from those around him. However, his calmness and knowledge are factors that earn him the trust of others even in difficult situations.

participants.private_seed: Every cycle the headline award looks the same size, yet what it actually buys keeps shrinking in some places and holding steady in others. Before ranking anything, I want to know which kinds of spending the agency still absorbs centrally and which now land on the awardee.

participants.name: Midori

persona.name: Midori
persona.personality: Midori has a calm and kind personality. She is friendly to everyone and listens to the concerns and problems of those around her, offering reliable advice. She can be a little shy, often acting reserved with people she meets for the first time, but once she opens up, she shows her bright and energetic side. She loves cooking and has a domestic side, but she also has a spirit of adventure and enjoys trying new things. She values balance in both her work and personal life and places importance on harmony with those around her.

participants.private_seed: Too many recent awards lost time to things that had nothing to do with the science itself, and the panel usually hears about it only after the money is committed. It seemed worth asking in advance where work in this field actually gets interrupted.

participants.name: Shizue

persona.name: Shizue
persona.personality: Shizue has a very calm and gentle personality. Even as she has grown older, she continues to smile warmly at those around her and is a very caring person. She is always considerate of others, friendly, and sometimes shows a playful side. She often reaches out to those who are feeling down with kind words and never hesitates to lend a helping hand when needed, which has earned her the affection of many people in the village and community. Through her years of life experience, Shizue has come to understand the importance of living peacefully with others.

participants.private_seed: Our judgements about promise have not aged well, and some of us have watched confident picks quietly stall while plainer ones kept earning their keep. Rather than trust that instinct once more, I went back through what finished awards here actually delivered and when.

participants.name: Victoria

persona.name: Victoria
persona.personality: Victoria is a calm and rational person, but at times her excessive thoughtfulness can create barriers between her and those around her. She is reserved in her emotional expressions and keenly observes the expressions and attitudes of others, trying to discern their inner thoughts. Because she does not express herself much, she often gives others the impression of being somewhat mysterious, but deep down she has a strong will and a determination to stick to her beliefs. At times, she may display expressions of anxiety or fear, but it is precisely in such moments that her true strength becomes evident.

participants.private_seed: Nothing funded here runs in isolation, since it lands on shared facilities and services that no single award pays to expand. Given how often that spare capacity has been the thing that gives way, I looked at what state those services are in right now.

participants.name: Ryuji

persona.name: Ryuji
persona.personality: Ryuji has a calm and cautious personality, and is the type of person who always assesses the situation before acting. He rarely shows his emotions, and spends his time thinking deeply about many things. His friends consider him to be serious and reliable, but his expressionless attitude can sometimes make them feel uneasy. He tends to judge things based on reason rather than intuition, and strongly sticks to his beliefs. He is very independent and often does things at his own pace.

participants.private_seed: Money can be voted through in an afternoon, while the trained hands a project needs take years to gather and can disappear in a season. That worry sent me to the question of who is genuinely available around here now, and who has already gone.

You are the writer of the discussion described below. You write out the discussion that the participants listed below take part in, under the rules and the flow given.

## Setting
Award of a national grant for basic research in the life sciences. A five-member review panel convened by a national funding agency deliberates over the proposals that reached the final round. One multi-year grant is awarded in this cycle. Participants: Benjamin, Midori, Shizue, Victoria and Ryuji. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Travel and bench-fee lines in the ledgers
- National computing agreement and facility day rates
- Incident logs on shared instrumentation
- Station records from partner field sites
- Closeout files of finished awards
- Portfolio review of schedule overruns
- Accreditation and bookings at shared facilities
- National repository deposit turnaround
- Staffing rolls for technical posts
- Minutes on secondments and crew strength

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Shizue, Ryuji, Victoria, Benjamin and Midori. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.
